newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Konsortium eyes goods distribution market.
newsitem.headline: Konsortium eyes goods distribution market.

text.p: Malaysian haulage firm Konsortium Perkapalan Bhd said on Wednesday it was setting up distribution centres throughout the country to cut the time to move goods around.

Konsortium plans to be the key source of goods for distribution, with independent truckers going to its centres to haul the products on paid commissions, said group executive chairman Mirzan Mahathir.
"What we are trying to do is to reduce the movement (of haulage trucks) and increasing the loads," he told reporters after the company's extraordinary general meeting (EGM).
"At this point, everybody is working for himself. There is duplication...and efficiencies crop up," Mirzan said of current industry practice of individual truckers looking out for their own interest.

At the EGM, shareholders approved the company's plan to privately place out 16.1 million new shares. About 98 million ringgit of proceeds from the placement would be used to set up key distribution centres at 12 major cities.
Total investment cost to set up the centres was estimated at 124.2 million ringgit, with Konsortium planning to finance the shortfall by internally generated funds and bank borrowings.
Mirzan, eldest son of Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, said Konsortium also plans to raise the use of information technology in the haulage business to raise efficiency.
